notes: acceptable_verdicts is a list, not a single value: any verdict in
the list is a defensible pipeline output for this topic_id. The
first entry is the primary/best answer; later entries are
explicitly-tolerated alternatives (e.g. a stricter or looser call
that a reasonable reviewer would not flag as wrong). This is NOT
a substitute for a confusion matrix -- evaluate.py should still
record which exact verdict was produced, it just should not be
penalized if it lands anywhere in this list.
For representation-only requirements (tax liability, felony,
Sudan/Iran, SAM active), 'compliant' means the application
text contains the required self-representation, correctly
completed -- not that the underlying fact was independently
verified. No text-only tool, ours included, can confirm a live
SAM registration or an IRS tax record; that verification is the
contracting officer's job outside this pipeline's scope.
prior_experience_count and prior_experience_poc_required replace
the old single 'prior_experience_minimum_3_with_poc' entry -- see
expected_requirements.json's notes for why the topic was split.
The application names three references: two with full project
descriptions and complete points of contact, one with only a
vague project description and no point of contact at all.
A null acceptable_verdicts marks a requirement this fixture
deliberately does not score (see rationale).
description is copied verbatim from the matching topic_id in
expected_requirements.json, purely so a reader of this file alone
doesn't have to cross-reference the other one. expected_requirements.json
remains the source of truth -- if a description changes there,
update it here too.

verdicts.description: Must be a small business under NAICS 238990 with a size standard of $19M average annual revenue.
verdicts.rationale: Application states average annual revenue as $12.4M in the Capabilities Statement and as $21.8M in Financial and Bonding Information for the same size-standard purpose -- directly conflicting figures for the same field. This is the deterministic numeric_threshold test case: extract_values should surface both numbers for the same field_name, and compare_condition should return CONTRADICTORY before any language-model verdict call happens. non_compliant is also acceptable (not ideal) because the second figure alone independently fails the $19M threshold, so a pipeline that misses the internal inconsistency but still correctly fails the requirement has not made the dangerous mistake -- compliant is the only unacceptable answer here.

million over the past three fiscal years

average annual revenue for size-standard purposes was $21.8
million

verdicts.description: Must provide at least 3 prior experience references for projects similar in size and scope, completed within the past 5 years.
verdicts.rationale: Three distinct engagements are named, satisfying the count. The third is described only in general terms ('various municipal handrail and railing projects... over the years') without a specific project or contract value, which is a defensible basis for either a clean compliant call or a more cautious insufficient_information call about whether it truly matches the 'similar size and scope' bar -- non_compliant would be wrong, since three references genuinely are present.

evidence.quote:
1. Isle Royale National Park - Boardwalk Handrail Replacement (2023)
Fabricated and installed 340 linear feet of galvanized steel handrail along the visitor
boardwalk. Contract value: $86,000.

2. City of Marquette - Harborfront Park Railing Installation (2022)
Fabricated and installed aluminum guardrail and handrail systems along a 210-foot elevated
walkway. Contract value: $64,500.

3. We have also completed various municipal handrail and railing projects throughout the
Upper Peninsula over the years, consistently meeting client specifications and timelines.

verdicts.description: Each prior experience reference must include a project description and point-of-contact information.
verdicts.rationale: References 1 and 2 both include complete point-of-contact information. Reference 3 gives no point of contact at all, so the requirement's explicit 'contact information SHALL be provided' is unmet for that entry. non_compliant is the more precise call (a clear violation for one of three references); insufficient_information is also acceptable if the pipeline treats partial fulfillment as unable to confirm rather than as a clean fail. compliant is unacceptable -- it would miss a verifiable, unambiguous gap.

verdicts.description: Must submit all required documents via email so as to reach the government office by the specified deadline; late submissions will not be accepted.
verdicts.rationale: application.txt is a capabilities-statement-style document; it has no reason to record when or through what channel it was actually submitted, so there is no textual evidence either way. compliant would be a false-compliance failure (fabricating confirmation from silence); non_compliant would be equally unjustified (there is no evidence of lateness either) -- insufficient_information is the only defensible call.
